items.excerpt: Save 40% Off the ASUS ZenScreen 16" 1080p Portable USB Monitor for Black Friday
items.content_text: It's no surprise why USB portable monitors are becoming so popular. They provide extra screen real estate for laptop users and they're much slimmer and lighter than your average monitor so you can carry them around. Many newer laptops now have USB ports that can power the monitor so that you don't even need to plug it into an outlet. In addition to boosting productivity on a laptop, the monitor also works as a totable display for your Nintendo Switch. Talk about convenience! For the final hours of Black Friday, Amazon is offering the ASUS ZenScreen 15.6" USB Portable Monitor (MB169CK) for just $69.67 with free shipping after a 40% off discount. There are many portable monitor brands out there, but ASUS is generally considered amongst the highest quality options, especially with its robust 3 year warranty. Save 40% Off the ASUS ZenScreen 16" Portable USB Monitor The ASUS ZenScreen (MB16AHV) is a portable 15.6" monitor that weighs just 2 pounds and measures less than 0.5 inches thin. The monitor features a built-in kickstand and a 1/4" threaded hole for attaching it to a tripod or table mount. The 15.6" IPS display features a 1080p resolution (141ppi), 60Hz refresh rate, wide 178-degree viewing angle, and an anti-glare matte surface. Connectivity options include two USB Type-C ports and one mini HDMI port to connect to a laptop, tablet, or handheld gaming PC for use as a main or secondary display. If your device is equipped with a USB Type-C output with Power Delivery, then a single cable can be used for both video and power. Otherwise, you'll need two cables: a mini HDMI or USB Type-C cable for video and a second USB Type-C cable to a wall charger for power. Compatible with Nintendo Switch or Steam Deck This monitor works quite well paired with a gaming handheld like the Nintendo Switch or Steam Deck. You will have to use the two-cable setup (one USB cable to the handheld, one USB cable to a wall charger) for this to work properly. The 1080p 60Hz panel best complements the Nintendo Switch, since the Switch only supports up to 720p @ 60Hz anyway. The Steam Deck and Switch 2 can support higher resolutions and refresh rates, but at that point you're really taxing your system, and 1080p/60Hz on a smaller display is an ideal balance between visual fidelity and playable framerates. items.title: Here Are the Top Black Friday 4K TV Deals You Don't Want to Miss, From Budget to Best
items.excerpt: Best prices of the year on top brands including LG, Samsung, Hisense, TCL, and more.
items.content_text: Whether you're looking for the TV with the best image quality and you've got money to spend, or you've got a tight budget and value is paramount, Black Friday has got you covered. If you're planning to upgrade to OLED this year, you'll find a deal for it. If you're looking for something bigger, like a 75" or dare I say 100", you'll find a deal for that too. The Best Black Friday TV Deals The Best OLED TV Deal LG's most popular OLED TV in 2026 is on sale for Black Friday. Amazon currently has the 65" LG Evo C6 4K OLED TV for $1,399.99 with free delivery. You also get $100 in bonus Amazon promotional credit that's automatically applied during checkout. Amazon Prime cardholders can get an additional 10% cashback (instead of 5%). The C6 is LG's current 2026 model in the LG's C-series OLED TV lineup. LG's C-series OLED TV in general has been our favorite TVs for console gaming for many years thanks to its outstanding image quality, low input lag, and high refresh rate. This is one of the best TVs you can get for streaming 4K HDR content in its intended glory. It boasts the near-infinite black levels, near-infinite contrast ratio, and near-instantaneous response times you'd expect from any OLED TV. The C6 is also equipped with modern gaming features including a native 120Hz panel that can be pushed to as high as 165Hz, HDMI 2.1 inputs, variable refresh rate and auto low latency mode. The Best Black Friday Budget TV Deal 65" model for $299.99 (was $550) 75" model for $379.99 (was $700) If you're looking for an affordable TV that offers solid image quality, the Hisense QD5 is hard to beat. For Black Friday, you can pick up a 55" model for under $200 or a 75" model for under $400. This 2026 Hisense TV offers great image quality that punches above its weight class thanks to Hisense's proprietary Hi-QLED panel with direct-lit LED backlighting. The QD5 officially supports a number of HDR formats including HDR10, Dolby Vision, and HLG. Roku smart interface is also integrated, which is considered one of the best built-in smart interfaces you can get from a budget TV. It's definitely a favorite of mine; I prefer it over Google TV and Fire TV. The Best Black Friday Budget Samsung TV Deal Not everyone feels comfortable buying a TV brand that isn't Samsung, LG, or Sony (although, technically, Sony TVs are now made by TCL). In that case, the best budget TV deal from one of these brands is easily the Samsung M80H TV . This is a new 2026 model TV that features a mini LED panel and a native 144Hz refresh rate so you can play supported PlayStation 5, Xbox, and PC games at up to 144fps. The 65" TV is currently less than $500 and you can't find many (any?) TVs in that price range that offer this level of features and a Samsung/LG/Sony brand name. If you want a really big screen, consider a projector instead If you're aiming for a TV that's bigger than 75", you might want to consider a projector instead. XGIMI makes wonderfully compact yet capable laser projectors in its Horizon series and they're discounted by up to 40% off during Black Friday. The Horizon projectors are easy enough to move around and you don't have to worry about an enormous black screen cluttering your wall when you're not using it. The Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV Gives OLED a Run for Its Money Last year, Hisense pioneered the first RGB Mini-LED TV with its 116UX model. Granted it was only available as a massive 116" screen that retailed for $20,000. In 2026, Hisense released its second generation RGB Mini-LED tech at a much more affordable price point with its UR-series lineup. For Black Friday, you can get it for even less. Best Buy has just discounted the 65" Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV from $2,000 all the way down to $899.99 and the 75" model from $2,500 down to $1399.99, both with free delivery. These are the lowest prices since launch and beats previous lows by $200. RGB Mini-LED is an evolution of Mini-LED technology. Traditional mini-LED TVs consist of an array of blue LED that are passed through RGB filters to produced the desired color. RGB Mini-LED TVs use red, green, and blue LEDs instead of just blue, which means the pixels no longer need filters to produce the desired color. The result is more accurate color reproduction, less blooming and, most importantly, a wider color gamut. Color gamut of RGB Mini-LED surpasses that of OLEDs, since current-generation OLEDs also use color filters combined with blue OLEDs. How does that translate in the real world? It means that you see richer, more accurate colors, smoother gradients and less banding than even OLEDs. TCL introduces its own SQD mini LED tech in the QM8L TV 75" model for $1,397.99 (was $3,000) 85" model for $2,297.99 (was $4,000) 98" model for $2,997.99 (was $6,000) One of the best new TVs of 2026 dropped to its lowest price ever ahead of Black Friday. The QM8L is a pretty significant upgrade over last year's QM8K model thanks to the introduction of TCL's highly-touted SQD technology. SQD - which stands for Super Quantum Dot - is a more refined version of QLED tech. Quantum dot panels have a layer of microscopic crystals measuring a few nanometers in size that are able to separate light into precise colors. SQD tech uses even smaller crystals - as small as a single nanometer in width. This allows SQD panels to pack in even more dimming zones, usually numbering in the thousands, which in turn produces a brighter image with higher contrast and richer colors. items.content_text: There are so many great Mario games to check out on the Nintendo Switch . This sale won't last long, and for just over $12, it's hard to beat what could be a great addition to your board game collection .

items.title: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair Dev's Explanation for Skipping Xbox Sparks Backlash
items.excerpt: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition developer Playtonic has come under fire from Xbox owners after it ruled out an Xbox Series X and S version of the rerelease.
items.content_text: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition developer Playtonic has come under fire from Xbox owners after it ruled out an Xbox Series X and S version of the rerelease. In a statement published online, the UK studio said it had to prioritize the PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 versions because the cost of bringing it to Xbox "just isn't viable for us at this time." The original game, released in 2018, launched on Xbox One at the same time as PlayStation 4 and Nintendo Switch. The next-gen upgrade hits PC, PS5, and Switch 2 only on December 15. "Unfortunately, we've had to prioritize our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the forseeable future," Playtonic said. "We understand the frustration felt by those of you who won't be able to access the Definnitive Edition at launch, but unfortunately the cost of bringing it to more platforms just isn't viable for us at this time. As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face. Please know that this wasn't an easy decision to make, and we apologize to any of you affected by this. "We only wish things were different, and we value every single one of you and your feedback." Playtonic's statement is light on specifics, but most are reading between the lines here and assuming what the studio is saying here is that it weighed up how much it would cost to port the rerelease to Xbox Series X and S against its potential return, and found the numbers didn't add up. "This means the game didn’t do meaningful numbers on the Xbox. It doesn’t make any sense otherwise," one person suggested . "They could’ve just said the game sold bad on Xbox and they don’t have enough money or time to justify updating it," another said . Whatever the reason, Xbox fans certainly aren't happy. "Slap in the face to Xbox fans who’ve supported you from the beginning," one Xbox user said . "Will not support you any longer or buy any future Playtonic games if we’re not gonna be treated equally." "It's a free upgrade for a game we've already brought. The same as the other platforms but you are treating us poorly," another added . "So no we don't understand. No matter how you slice it, it's a **** you to Xbox buyers." "So... you can't afford to make a FREE upgrade for Xbox... but you could afford it for every other platform?" one person asked . "Well... won't be buying anything of yours from this point on. So there's even less money for you." "I could buy this game on PS5 or Switch but it’s clear you don’t want or deserve my support," another said.

items.excerpt: RGB Mini-LED tech boasts richer colors, a brighter picture, and wider viewing angles than ever before.
items.content_text: Last year, Hisense pioneered the first RGB Mini-LED TV with its 116UX model. Granted it was only available as a massive 116" screen that retailed for $20,000. In 2026, Hisense released its second generation RGB Mini-LED tech at a much more affordable price point with its UR-series lineup. For Black Friday, you can get it for even less. Best Buy has just discounted the 65" Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV from $2,000 all the way down to $899.99 and the 75" model from $2,500 down to $1399.99, both with free delivery. These are the lowest prices since launch and beats previous lows by $200. The Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV Gives OLED a Run for Its Money RGB Mini-LED is essentially the next generation evolution of Mini-LED technology. Traditional mini-LED TVs consist of an array of blue LED that are passed through RGB filters to produced the desired color. RGB Mini-LED TVs use red, green, and blue LEDs instead of just blue, which means the pixels no longer need filters to produce the desired color. The result is more accurate color reproduction, less blooming and, most importantly, a wider color gamut. In fact, the color gamut of RGB Mini-LED surpasses that of OLEDs, since current-generation OLEDs also use color filters combined with blue OLEDs. How does that translate in the real world? It means that you see richer, more accurate colors, smoother gradients and less banding than even OLEDs, especially in 4K HDR content. RGB Mini-LED TVs have several other features that out-class standard Mini-LEDs. They're brighter (far brighter than OLED TVs), making them perfect for daytime watching in bright rooms with little light control. items.content_text: If you're looking for a value-priced Apple laptop for basic everyday tasks like browsing, media streaming, word processing, and the like, then the recently released MacBook Neo is right up your alley. It's not as powerful as the M5 chip found in the MacBook Air , but as a result the Neo is nearly half the price. It's certainly capable enough to handle all of your daily tasks and it still supports AI and Apple Intelligence features. After all, no one's getting a MacBook for gaming anyway. The MacBook Neo features a 13" 2408x1506 (219ppi) Liquid Retina display, Apple A18 Pro chip with 6-core CPU, 5-core GPU, and 16-core NPU, 8GB of unified RAM, and a 256GB SSD. It measures about 0.5" thin and weighs in at 2.7 pounds. The chassis is 90% aluminum. Connectivity options include two USB-C ports, headphone jack, Wi-Fi 6E, and bluetooth. IGN's Jackie Thomas gave the MacBook Neo a glowing 9/10 review , stating that it is "without a doubt, the best budget laptop you can buy today."
